title: Offline-first SDK adaptors for hosted API: progressive buffering & tool-queue PRD (draft)
body:
Summary:
This PRD sketch defines an offline-first adaptor layer for the Hosted API SDKs (initial mobile/edge focus) that preserves streaming semantics, supports queued tool calls, and guarantees structured output validation when network connectivity is intermittent. The goal is to enable app developers to build resilient UX for low/spotty connectivity without re-implementing fallback logic or losing developer ergonomics for tool integration.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Many customer scenarios (mobile field apps, kiosks, sales tools, remote sites) experience intermittent connectivity. Current Hosted API streaming and tool-calling semantics assume always-online sockets or blocking retries.
- Developers end up building bespoke buffering layers, diverging UX, and inconsistent structured output validation.
- We lose observability and cost predictability when clients implement naive retries or duplicated requests.

Key goals:
- Provide an SDK-level offline adaptor that:
  - Preserves progressive/incremental output semantics (clients should be able to render partial responses when available).
  - Queues tool-calls locally and reliably delivers them when connectivity returns, with idempotency guarantees.
  - Validates structured output locally where possible (schema checks, lightweight sampling) and surfaces mismatches before network send.
  - Exposes simple developer primitives (startSession, resumeSession, enqueueToolCall, onProgress) that match Hosted API mental model.
- Ensure telemetry and cost accounting remain accurate (client-side counters + server reconciliation).
- Roll out as opt-in SDK feature initially (mobile JS/Android/iOS), with server-side support for resumable session tokens.

Non-goals:
- Not a full offline compute stack or authoritative local model execution (no on-device inference beyond small validators).
- Not a replacement for Dedicated/Private offline deployments.

User personas / scenarios:
- Field survey app: inspector collects notes, triggers an address-normalization tool call; connectivity lost mid-generation — UX shows partial summary and queues the tool call until online.
- Sales CRM mobile: agent composes a draft email summary using structured output templates; network flaps — SDK should persist intermediate deltas and reconcile once online.
- Kiosk agent: intermittent bursts of connectivity; ability to continue servicing users with graceful degradation and eventual sync.

High-level design:
1) Session model and resumability
  - startLocalSession(): SDK creates a local session id + ephemeral state.
  - hosted startSessionOnServer(token): server issues a resumable session token that can be used later to stitch partial outputs.
  - resumeSession(token): SDK attempts to reconnect and reconcile local buffered frames with server state.
  - Conflict policy: last-client-write-wins for non-authoritative deltas; tool-call results are reconciled via idempotency keys.

2) Progressive frame format (JSONL-friendly, compact)
  - Frames are line-delimited small payloads: metadata header, incremental text and structured deltas, and optional tool-call markers.
  - Minimal frame example (conceptual):
    [frame-id]\t[type:text|structured|tool-call|checkpoint]\t[session-v]\t[payload-base64-or-utf8]
  - Frames are append-only locally; checkpoints mark safe replay points for server-side stitching.

3) Local tool queue and execution semantics
  - enqueueToolCall(toolName, args, idempotencyKey): persists the call in local queue.
  - Delivery attempts use exponential backoff + network-awareness; SDK tags delivery attempts with client telemetry.
  - Server returns definitive result; SDK attempts to merge tool outputs into the session stream on resume.
  - If the same idempotencyKey is observed server-side, server responds with cached result to avoid double-execution.

4) Structured output validation and light linting
  - SDK ships lightweight validators (JSON Schema subset) to catch obvious structural mismatches before send.
  - When mismatch detected, SDK surfaces a developer callback: onSchemaError(frame, suggestions).
  - Optional local auto-correct heuristics (e.g., missing fields with defaults) behind a flag.

5) Streaming semantics and UX expectations
  - While offline, onProgress events are fired from local frames (as they are produced by client or buffered responses).
  - When connectivity resumes, SDK attempts an ordered replay of frames, streaming server responses appended to what client has already shown.
  - Roll-forward vs roll-back options: by default we prefer roll-forward stitching (append server-completed tokens); provide opt-in roll-back if strict canonical server output required.

6) Telemetry and billing reconciliation
  - Client emits local counters: tokens-produced-local, tool-queue-length, delivery-attempts.
  - On server reconciliation, server provides final token/billing deltas; SDK pushes reconciliation event to the console.
  - Telemetry should allow SRE/billing to attribute cost to eventual server execution, with flags for suspected duplicate attempts.

SDK ergonomics / API surface (proposal)
- startSession(opts?): returns localSessionId, optional resumableToken when server handshake succeeds.
- appendLocalDelta(delta, type="text"|"structured"): writes a frame to local store and emits onProgress locally.
- enqueueToolCall(tool, args, opts?): returns toolCallId; stores idempotencyKey and emits onToolQueued.
- resumeAndSync(resumableToken): reconnect + ordered replay + reconciliation.
- onProgress(cb), onToolResult(cb), onSchemaError(cb), onSyncStatus(cb) — simple event hooks.
- Convenience flows: showPartialThenPatch(serverPatch), autoMergeMode(true|false).

Server changes required (sketch):
- Resumable session tokens and frame-stitch API that accepts ordered frames from client and returns canonical appended tokens.
- Tool-call idempotency index and snapshotting to return cached results for repeated deliveries.
- Reconciliation endpoint that returns final billing/token counts and a mapping of frames->serverTokens.

Data storage and security considerations:
- Local frames encrypted at rest using platform keystore (Android Keystore / iOS Keychain).
- Opt-in user data retention policies and TTL for queued tool calls.
- For regulated customers, provide configuration to disable local persistence (server-only).

Backward compatibility and migration
- Default to no-op for existing SDK users; opt-in flag to enable adaptor.
- Fall back to normal streaming when persistent storage unavailable.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (research): 2 weeks — prototype JS mobile adaptor reading/writing frames to IndexedDB and testing resume flows with test harness.
- Phase 1 (alpha): 6 weeks — expose APIs in mobile SDKs, server-side stitch endpoint MVP, basic telemetry. Invite 2-3 customers.
- Phase 2 (beta): 8 weeks — refine schema validation, idempotency guarantees, add desktop JS and Android/iOS native optimizations.
- Phase 3 (GA): 4 weeks — general availability, docs, migration guides, console reconciliation UI.

Success metrics
- Developer adoption: number of apps enabled with adaptor (target 10 early customers during beta).
- Reliability: reduction in duplicate tool executions reported by server (target 90% fewer duplicates for enrolled apps).
- UX: % of user sessions with graceful resume vs hard-failure (target 80% graceful resume).
- Observability: reconciliation events emitted within 1 minute of resume in 95% of cases.

Open questions / TODOs
- Server: should we accept partial frames out-of-order and reorder server-side, or force strict client ordering? Pros/cons discussion needed.
- Schema validation scope: how many validators to ship vs lean SDK? Performance trade-offs on low-end devices.
- Billing model: how to attribute costs for queued executions that get deduplicated at server? Need finance input.
- UX guidelines: mobile designers need patterns for showing partial output vs transitory placeholders.

Immediate next steps
- Spike: Jonas to build a small IndexedDB + frame-replay prototype and a test harness that simulates flaky connectivity (2 weeks).
- Backend design: Lina to draft frame-stitch API contract and idempotency index design (1 week).
- SDK API review: Aisha + Devon to iterate on minimal primitives and a short sample app demonstrating an inspector flow (1 week).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally focused on SDK ergonomics and developer experience; we should avoid over-optimizing server complexity in the first iteration.
- Look for places where we can reuse existing session/resume work (dedicated session tokens already in roadmap).
- Feedback: prioritize simple, testable semantics over perfect theoretical guarantees for phase 1.

End of draft.
